openings.claim: Remove the hypothesized necessity of reconciling local timestamps before reporting divergence. The supplied export-before-parse anomaly permits a counterexample: an evidence ledger can organize supported stage boundaries without repairing clock order.
openings.delta: Changed dependency: timestamp reconciliation. Changed action: compare corresponding recorded input/output digests in manifest stage order. Carrier: the supplied local script or spreadsheet plus a record-linked ledger. Retain digest comparison. Treat the manifest as expected order, never proof of execution; ambiguous ordering or correspondence produces an explicit unresolved interval.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, timestamp-first sorting followed by manual anomaly reconciliation, removal should allow a supported boundary or interval despite the anomalous timestamp. After transform-record removal, support may weaken and intervals widen; no missing record proves nonexecution. Differing observations are frozen localization, unresolved intervals and manual inspection counts. This does not establish that timestamps are generally unnecessary, or that reconciliation cannot help.
openings.probe: Run the removal workflow and timestamp-first rival on the two disjoint three-pair subsets within sixty analyst minutes plus twenty comparison minutes. Log every manual record inspection and cap each pair at twelve. Freeze all six reports, record references and resource-fitting next checks before opening the two sealed answer sheets. Compare supported localization and intervals against their supplied answers; separately examine the timestamp anomaly and final-review transform removals. Disjoint subsets limit causal attribution.
assumptions: Every definite stage claim cites a supplied record; explanations remain separate from observed digest mismatches.
Defeat condition: manifest order cannot establish relevant boundary order, or corresponding digest boundaries cannot be identified; retain an unresolved interval instead of claiming a stage.
Capacity condition: twelve manual inspections suffice to inspect cited support; otherwise unresolved output must state the remaining uncertainty and a next check within available records and time.
Whether removal improves localization or effort is uncertain; this is a bounded probe, not deployment.

assessment: One live removal opening. The timestamp anomaly challenges a prerequisite, while missing transform evidence requires bounded uncertainty rather than reconstruction or invented execution history.
